topic: Mistral Large 4 vs the Chinese open-weight leaders: what the model card actually scores, and the memory wall for home PCs
title: Mistral Large 4 "beats Chinese models"? The card says tied
description: Mistral Large 4 open weights landed and the CEO says it beats the Chinese models. We read the model card: coding tied at 48%, cyber ahead at 51%, aggregate index behind at 26, and the smallest quant is 233 GB. You will learn how to check a benchmark claim yourself. (Narration is AI-generated.)

narration_full: The Mistral headline isn't the receipt. The card is. Twenty-six on the index, one blended score of benchmarks; your gaming PC or Mac saw the headline. Chinese leaders score higher. Mistral Large four landed yesterday: open weights, the downloadable numbers a model is made of. The claim named no models or benchmarks. The card, the page beside the weights, prints forty-eight percent on coding: tied with GLM five point three. Cyber index: fifty-one percent, ahead. The catch: the Artificial Analysis index is somebody's chosen bucket; trading it for one win cherry-picks back. Smallest quant, the tightest squeeze, two hundred thirty-three gigabytes of weights; your gaming PC can't hold it. Tonight, open the card before the headline: which benchmark, which model, whose measurement?
